core_obligations: Variable rule (proof line 866): the last rule is bredpar1; the author marks this base case Exercise - it is the identity instance where M' = M = bcd(M) for a variable.
Abstraction (lines 867-871): M = lambda x.N, M' = lambda x.N'; bcd unfolds via bcd2 and the claim follows from bredpar2 plus the induction hypothesis.

Application (lines 872-883): M = PQ, M' = P'Q'; two subcases on whether P is an abstraction - if yes the redex is contracted through bredpar4 with both induction hypotheses; if no, bredpar3 applies and bcd3 identifies bcd(P)bcd(Q) with bcd(PQ).

Redex contraction (lines 884-890): M = (lambda x.N)Q, M' = N'[Q'/x]; lem:comp glues the hypotheses N' bredpar bcd(N) and Q' bredpar bcd(Q) into Subst{N'}{Q'}{x} bredpar Subst{bcd N}{bcd Q}{x} = bcd(M).
proof_roadmap: Invert on the last rule of the derivation of M bredpar M'.
For the variable case appeal to reflexivity of the development.
For lambda and application push the induction hypotheses through the bcd defining equations.
For the contracted redex invoke the substitution lemma lem:comp.
difficulty_reason: The completeness lemma for the beta-complete development in Tait's route to Church-Rosser (statement 860-862, proof 863-891). Four-rule derivation induction with one genuine sub-case split and one invocation of the substitution lemma; the variable rule is a trivial identity left as a one-word Exercise, every other case fully written. H2: standard but bookkeeping-heavy parallel-reduction induction.
